applicationSummary: A web-based agentic analytics application for the retail scenario that lets users ask natural-language questions over unified customer, product, order, invoice, payment, and location data. The solution uses Microsoft Fabric as the governed data foundation and Microsoft Foundry/Agent Framework for orchestration, with a React frontend and backend API that support conversational querying, chart/table outputs, chat history, and session persistence.
deploymentPrerequisites: Azure subscription with permission to create resource groups, app registrations, and assign RBAC roles at the resource group/subscription level.
Fabric capacity (F2+) and tenant settings enabled for Ontology (preview), Graph (preview), and Copilot and Azure OpenAI Service.
Regional availability for Microsoft Fabric, Azure AI Foundry, GPT model capacity, Azure Container Apps, and Azure Container Registry; the docs list examples such as East US.
Azure Developer CLI azd 1.15.0+ (and note azd 1.23.9 requires provision.preflight off).
PowerShell 7+, Bicep CLI 0.33.0+, Python 3.9+, Docker Desktop, Git, and Microsoft ODBC Driver 17 for local/deployment workflows.
If using VS Code Web, Azure CLI device-code authentication is required instead of browser-based az login.
For post-deployment data/build steps, access to the deployed Azure resources and a signed-in Azure account with Foundry User role if running locally against Foundry services.
businessScenarios: Retail sales analysis and product performance exploration using natural-language questions over unified customer, product, and sales data.
Retail inventory and sales operations with insights such as top-performing products, revenue over time, and segment growth.
Interactive charting and tabular analytics for business users who need quick answers without building dashboards.
Conversational access to governed enterprise data from a web application backed by Fabric and Azure AI services.
deploymentChecks: Confirm the deployed site opens successfully at the provided App Service URL and the application shell renders.
Verify the user is authenticated and that the UI reflects the signed-in identity/menu state after session establishment.
Send a retail question using the Send button and verify a response appears.
Send the same or another retail question by pressing Enter and verify the message submits.
Ask at least one question that should return a text response and confirm the assistant displays readable narrative output.
Ask a retail question that should return a chart and confirm chart rendering in the conversation.

If repository documents or guidance are exposed as citations in the app, ask a question grounded in the supplied retail policy/reference material and verify citations appear; do not use structured-data-only prompts for citation validation.
Start a new chat and verify the conversation resets without affecting prior persisted chats.
Show and hide the conversation history panel and verify the UI toggles correctly.
Select an existing conversation from history and verify the prior thread loads.

Rename a conversation, cancel a rename, delete a conversation, cancel a delete, clear all conversations, and cancel clear-all confirmation; treat clear-all as destructive and use only a dedicated isolated test identity.
Refresh or reopen the app and verify conversation persistence across reload/session restoration.
Validate that the user menu is accessible and that the app remains stable during basic navigation actions.
samplePrompts: Show total revenue by year for the last 5 years as a line chart.
Which segments show the highest YoY growth?
Show the top 10 products by revenue in the last year.
Show top 5 products by total quantity sold last month.

smokeTests.name: Authentication and session establishment
smokeTests.expectedResult: The application opens in an authenticated or sign-in-ready state and establishes a session for the current user without requiring credential automation or sign-out.

smokeTests.name: Authenticated UI shell loads
smokeTests.expectedResult: After authentication, the main application shell loads successfully with the retail experience visible and ready for interaction.

smokeTests.name: User identity menu is available
smokeTests.expectedResult: The signed-in user identity/menu control is visible and can be opened to inspect account-related options without requiring sign-out.

smokeTests.name: Application shell page load
smokeTests.expectedResult: The page loads without blocking errors and the primary chat workspace, input area, and supporting layout are visible.

smokeTests.name: Send message by button
smokeTests.expectedResult: Clicking Send submits the message and the conversation displays an assistant response for the retail question.

smokeTests.name: Send message by Enter
smokeTests.prompt: Show total revenue by year for the last 5 years.
smokeTests.expectedResult: Pressing Enter submits the message from the input box and the conversation displays a response.

smokeTests.name: Text response rendering
smokeTests.prompt: Which segments show the highest YoY growth?
smokeTests.expectedResult: The assistant returns a readable text-based answer in the conversation stream.

smokeTests.name: Chart response rendering
smokeTests.prompt: Show total revenue by year for the last 5 years as a line chart.
smokeTests.expectedResult: The assistant returns a chart visualization and it renders successfully in the response area.

smokeTests.name: Citation rendering from repository documents
smokeTests.prompt: According to the deployment guide, what is the default scenario used when no scenario is specified?
smokeTests.expectedResult: The response includes citations or reference markers grounded in the supplied deployment documentation, and the answer reflects the documented retail default scenario.

smokeTests.name: New chat starts a fresh conversation
smokeTests.expectedResult: Starting a new chat clears the current thread state and begins a fresh conversation without deleting prior history.

smokeTests.name: Show and hide chat history
smokeTests.expectedResult: The chat history panel can be shown and hidden, revealing prior conversations when visible.

smokeTests.name: Select conversation from history
smokeTests.expectedResult: Selecting a prior conversation loads that thread and its messages into the main chat area.

smokeTests.name: Rename conversation
smokeTests.expectedResult: A conversation can be renamed and the updated title is reflected in the history list.

smokeTests.name: Cancel rename conversation
smokeTests.expectedResult: Cancelling rename leaves the conversation title unchanged.

smokeTests.name: Delete conversation
smokeTests.expectedResult: Deleting a conversation removes it from the history list after confirmation.

smokeTests.name: Cancel delete conversation
smokeTests.expectedResult: Cancelling delete keeps the conversation in history and no removal occurs.

smokeTests.name: Clear all conversations
smokeTests.expectedResult: Clear-all confirmation is presented and, when confirmed in an isolated test identity, all conversations are removed from history.

smokeTests.name: Cancel clear all conversations
smokeTests.expectedResult: Cancelling the clear-all confirmation leaves all existing conversations intact.

smokeTests.name: Conversation persistence across reload
smokeTests.expectedResult: Existing conversations and session context remain available after a page refresh or app reload.

smokeTests.name: Open chat history
smokeTests.expectedResult: The chat history panel is visible.

playwrightRecommendations: Use a dedicated isolated test identity for destructive history-clear validation.
Prefer stable UI assertions such as visible controls, conversation count changes, and presence of response containers over exact model wording.
For chat submissions, verify both the submitted user message and the appearance of an assistant response before checking content type.
Use the retail-specific prompts from the deployment guide to avoid relying on unsupported or scenario-mismatched content.
If the app exposes citations only for document-grounded answers, keep the citation test aligned to repository docs and avoid structured-data-only prompts.
Prefer resilient selectors for chat input, send button, history drawer, conversation items, rename/delete controls, and confirmation dialogs.
Allow extra time for session establishment and initial model response generation, especially on first load after deployment.
For chart prompts, assert that a chart canvas/SVG/visual container renders rather than validating every datapoint label.
